title: Break sensors↔ghost cyclic dependency
description:
sensors/GhostMotionPipeline imports ghost/tuningConfig (line 26) and ghost/GhostCalibrationPage imports sensors/GhostMotionPipeline (line 7), creating a module-level cycle. Neither module can be tested or deployed independently. This is a structural blocker — any extraction touching sensors or ghost depends on this being resolved first.

Implementation:
- Move TuningConfig from ghost/tuningConfig.ts to src/shared/tuningConfig.ts (or src/shared/ghost/)
- Update imports in sensors/GhostMotionPipeline.ts and ghost/GhostCalibrationPage.ts
- Verify no remaining cross-imports between sensors/ and ghost/

Done when: `import-cycles` (or equivalent) reports zero cycles between sensors/ and ghost/; both modules' unit tests pass without importing from the other.
notes:
Source: modularity diagnostic 2026-05-19, Finding 2; rule-of-5-universal review CORR-001/EDGE-001.
Verification command: npx madge --circular src/ should report no sensors<->ghost cycle (or fewer overall cycles if unrelated ones remain).
Preferred target: src/shared/tuningConfig.ts.

title: Sync GhostCalibrationPage correctness before pipeline extraction
description:
Four pre-extraction bugs in src/ghost/GhostCalibrationPage.ts that must be fixed before GhostMotionPipeline extraction, or the pipeline would inherit incorrect behaviour:

1. Double gyro integration (CRITICAL) — devicemotion handler AND onGyroReading both call feedGhostGyro, causing 2× yaw/pitch accumulation. Remove the call from the devicemotion handler; keep only the one in onGyroReading.

2. scanAxis hard-coded to 'y' — onGyroReading uses literal 'y' instead of getOrientation() like GhostOverlayCanvas does. Replace with getOrientation()-based lookup.

3. Missing clampYawToViewport — GhostOverlayCanvas clamps yaw; calibration page does not. Add the same call after yaw integration so both behave identically during long scans.

4. Duplicate focalLengthPx — defined separately in GhostCalibrationPage and ghostOverlay.ts. Move to a single exported constant (e.g. src/sensors/ghostConstants.ts) consumed by both before extraction so GhostMotionPipeline inherits the canonical value.

All four changes are in the same file or adjacent constants file; fixing together is more efficient than four separate PRs with no standalone demo value.

title: Fix double gyro integration in GhostCalibrationPage
description: Each physical devicemotion event causes feedGhostGyro to be called twice — once by the devicemotion handler and once by onGyroReading — doubling the yaw/pitch accumulation rate. This is a critical correctness bug that must be fixed before extracting GhostMotionPipeline or the pipeline would inherit 2x integration. Fix: remove the redundant call so each event integrates exactly once.

title: Camera permission prep and denied-camera recovery for quick start
description:
## Why
Creating the session is not enough; users need clear camera-permission preparation and a recoverable denied-camera path after quick start.

## End-to-end behavior
After quick-start creation succeeds and the capture route opens, `CaptureView` shows **Allow camera access to photograph shelf spines.** before the first camera request settles. If permission is denied or the camera is unavailable, `CaptureView` explains that camera access is required, and Back returns home to an enabled **Start scanning** action while keeping the created session visible in **Previous scans**.

## Scope
- `CaptureView` permission-prep messaging and startup sequence
- Denied/unavailable camera error messaging and back-navigation behavior
- Home/capture integration tests in the `CaptureView` and home-route test suites for permission-prep and recovery path

## Acceptance criteria

- The permission request remains part of the user-initiated start flow
- Denied/unavailable camera path shows a clear camera-required error
- Back from the denied/unavailable state returns home with enabled **Start scanning**
- The created session remains visible under **Previous scans** after returning home
- This issue does **not** own Pending/Exported status wording; that belongs to `mibilioteca-62mr`

title: Quick start shows pending/error states and prevents duplicate creates
description:
## Why
Quick start needs trustworthy recovery behavior. Users must see pending/error states, and retries must not create duplicate scans when success evidence already exists.

## End-to-end behavior
After **Start scanning** is tapped, the user sees **Starting camera…** and cannot double-submit. If creation fails, the home screen shows the recovery error and restores **Start scanning**. If a prior attempt already produced usable success evidence, retry navigates/resumes instead of creating a duplicate scan.

## Scope
- Home quick-start state machine and disabled/pending UI
- Standard error handling for remote failure and local persistence failure
- Retry logic using in-memory `CreateScanResult` and persisted IndexedDB session evidence
- Tests for duplicate-prevention, partial persistence failure, and retry behavior

## Acceptance criteria
- Pending state changes button text to **Starting camera…** and disables the action
- Failure state shows **Couldn’t start scan. Check connection/storage and try again.** and restores an enabled **Start scanning** button
- Partial failure where remote create succeeds but local persistence fails shows the same recovery error
- Retry checks in-memory or persisted success evidence before issuing another create mutation
- Tests prove duplicate creates are not issued solely due to retry after interrupted success

## Traceability
- OpenSpec: `openspec/changes/add-quick-start-scan/specs/capture-start-ux/spec.md`
- Requirements: Quick-start pending and retry behavior
- Tasks: 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 2.4, 3.1

## Delivery approach
Apply TDD and Tidy First: write failing tests for pending, failure, and ambiguous retry paths first; implement the smallest safe state transitions; extract a typed helper only if duplication appears.

On a real mobile device this makes the orientation model selector and reset actions unreliable to tap. title: [SpecMismatch] Blur scoring operates on full-res ImageData, not 320x240 downscale
description: Spec (add-capture-metrics/specs/image-quality/spec.md, 'Zero-Allocation Blur Scoring'): blur score SHALL be computed on a 320x240 downscaled image. Code (src/tracer/qualityChecks.ts:24 runQualityChecks, src/tracer/imageProcessing.ts laplacianVariance): laplacianVariance is called directly on the full-resolution ImageData passed in. No downscaling step exists. This violates both the zero-allocation requirement (full-res is larger) and the fixed 320x240 input size.
close_reason: downscaleImageData implemented and wired into runQualityChecks; all tests green

title: [SpecMismatch] imuMath.ts file path matches spec but estimateDisplacement uses gravity from grx/gry/grz, spec says GravitySensor
description: Spec (add-capture-metrics/specs/imu-displacement/spec.md): displacement uses quaternion rotation and GravitySensor readings (grx/gry/grz) for gravity subtraction. Code (src/sensors/imuMath.ts:42-45): subtracts curr.grx/gry/grz from curr.ax/ay/az before rotating — gravity is applied in device frame before rotation, not in world frame after. This is mathematically incorrect: gravity should be subtracted in world frame post-rotation, or the device-frame gravity sensor components should be used without additional rotation.
close_reason: rotateVec called on raw accel first, then gravity subtracted in world frame; RED test with 90° pitch device exposed the bug

title: [SpecMismatch] displacementMeters computed in shutter.ts but CaptureView.takePhoto bypasses shutter()
description: Spec (add-capture-metrics/specs/imu-displacement/spec.md, 'Inter-Shot Displacement Estimation'): CaptureRecord.qualityChecks.displacementMeters SHALL be estimated via imuTrace slice. Code: src/tracer/shutter.ts correctly implements this via getImuSlice, but src/tracer/CaptureView.ts:399-470 (takePhoto) calls createCaptureRecord directly, never calls shutter(), and never provides getImuSlice — so displacementMeters is always undefined in the live capture path.
close_reason: displacementMeters now populated in takePhoto via getImuSlice; cross-session reset handled by setCameraState guard

title: [SpecMismatch] Translation shift NOT applied to canvas transform
description: Spec (add-translation-tracking/specs/ghost-overlay/spec.md, 'Gyro-Driven Horizontal Shift'): totalShiftX = rotShiftX + transShiftX, totalShiftY = rotShiftY + transShiftY applied via translate3d. Code (src/sensors/ghostOverlayCanvas.ts:111-118): canvas transform uses only computeShiftPx(yawRad) and computeShiftPy(pitchRad). computeTranslationShiftPx/computeTranslationShiftPy exist in ghostOverlay.ts but are never called from GhostOverlayCanvas or GhostMotionPipeline — translation component is fully absent from the rendered shift.

title: [SpecMismatch] ZUPT uses exponential decay, not hard-zero on gate close
description: Spec (add-translation-tracking/specs/ghost-overlay/spec.md, 'ZUPT Drift Correction'): velX and velY SHALL be set to 0 when |omega| rises above hide threshold (0.55 rad/s). Code (src/sensors/ghostOverlay.ts:128-131 zeroVelocity, src/sensors/GhostMotionPipeline.ts): the gate-close path does NOT call zeroVelocity at all — it only emits gateOpen:false. The accel ZUPT in feedGhostAccel uses exponential decay (tau=200ms), not hard-zero. Spec scenario 'Velocity clamped when gate closes' is unimplemented.

title: [Robustness] imuRecorder buffer grow() doubles unboundedly with no max cap
description: In src/sensors/imuRecorder.ts, grow() doubles the Float32Array capacity each time rowCount reaches capacity, with no upper limit. At 60 Hz primary sensor, INITIAL_CAPACITY=1024 fills in ~17 s. After ~34 min of recording the buffer exceeds 128 MB (131072 rows × 14 fields × 4 bytes). On low-memory devices this triggers OOM termination. There is no max-capacity guard or write-to-storage chunking to bound peak RSS.

title: [SpecMismatch] Out-of-range distance param silently discarded, no console warning
description: Spec (add-distance-config/specs/ghost-overlay/spec.md, Scenario 'Out-of-range URL param is rejected'): when x<20 or x>150 the value SHALL be clamped AND a console warning emitted. Code (src/sensors/ghostOverlayCanvas.ts:52): out-of-range values are silently replaced with default 60 (not clamped to nearest bound). No console.warn is ever called. Also contradicts add-translation-tracking spec which requires clamping, not replacement.

title: [SpecMismatch] No tilt sanity warning overlay for non-upright phone
description: Spec (add-distance-config/specs/ghost-overlay/spec.md, 'Tilt Sanity Warning'): capture view SHALL display a non-blocking overlay 'Hold phone upright for best alignment' when |beta-90|>30° for >1 second, suppressed before first capture. Code: no such overlay exists in src/tracer/CaptureView.ts. The quality poll only computes tiltDegrees for qualityChecks and shows a generic 'tilted' badge — this is unrelated to the beta-based upright check and has no 1-second debounce or first-capture suppression.

title: [SpecMismatch] Working distance NOT persisted to localStorage
description: Spec (add-distance-config/specs/ghost-overlay/spec.md, 'Working Distance Configuration'): value SHALL be persisted under localStorage key miblioteca.workingDistanceCm. Spec also requires slider that persists on change. Code (src/tracer/CaptureView.ts:271-276): distance is read from URL param only, never written to localStorage. No slider exists. The localStorage key miblioteca.workingDistanceCm is never read or written anywhere in src/.

title: [SpecMismatch] getDebugState() omits workingDistanceCm from ghost payload
description: Spec (add-distance-config/specs/ghost-overlay/spec.md, 'Working Distance in Debug Log'): ghost object in capture:shutter MUST include workingDistanceCm as a number. Code (src/sensors/ghostOverlayCanvas.ts:192-215): getDebugState() returns shiftPx, shiftPy, rotShiftPx, rotShiftPy, yawIntegral, pitchIntegral, visible, displayWidth, displayHeight — workingDistanceCm field is never included.

title: [SpecMismatch] ghost:at-shutter missing dx_cm, dy_cm, velX, velY, workingDistanceCm
description: Spec (add-translation-tracking/specs/ghost-overlay/spec.md, 'Translation Debug Events'): capture:shutter nested ghost object MUST include dx_cm, dy_cm, velX, velY, workingDistanceCm. Code (src/tracer/CaptureView.ts:420-424): capture:shutter logs only ghost.getDebugState() which returns shiftPx, shiftPy, rotShiftPx, rotShiftPy, yawIntegral, pitchIntegral, visible, displayWidth, displayHeight — no translation state at all.

title: [SpecMismatch] ghost:shift missing dx_cm, dy_cm, velX, velY fields
description: Spec (add-translation-tracking/specs/ghost-overlay/spec.md, 'Translation Debug Events'): ghost:shift event payload MUST include dx_cm, dy_cm, velX, velY numeric fields. Code (src/sensors/ghostOverlayCanvas.ts:122-128): ghost:shift only logs shiftPx, shiftPy, yawIntegral, pitchIntegral, displayWidth, displayHeight. Translation state is entirely absent from the payload.

title: [Robustness] ghost/main.ts constructs Gyroscope without try/catch; throws on permission denial
description: In src/ghost/main.ts lines 8-10, new Gyroscope({ frequency: 60 }) is called unconditionally if window.Gyroscope exists. The Generic Sensor API constructor throws a DOMException (NotAllowedError) when sensor permission has been denied. There is no try/catch, so an unhandled exception crashes the entire ghost page before GhostCalibrationPage is even constructed.

title: [Robustness] GhostMotionPipeline sets gyro onerror to null, crashes silently
description: In src/sensors/GhostMotionPipeline.ts line 55, gyro.onerror is set to null. A sensor error during the ghost overlay session (hardware fault, permission loss) is discarded. The pipeline continues requesting RAF frames, the overlay freezes at its last position with no indication to the user, and no cleanup occurs.

title: [Robustness] imuRecorder silently discards sensor errors (onerror set to null)
description: In src/sensors/imuRecorder.ts, all four sensors (accel, gyro, absOri, grav) have their onerror handler explicitly set to null (lines 94, 105, 116, 127). If a sensor fires an error event (e.g. permission revoked mid-session, hardware fault), the error is swallowed with no user feedback and no session-stop. The recording continues writing stale last-known values indefinitely.

title: [MissingSpec] Ghost calibration page has no OpenSpec change
description: The /ghost calibration page (GhostCalibrationPage.ts, ghost/main.ts, ghost/types.ts) is fully implemented — 4-phase state machine (IDLE→RECORDING→REPOSITIONING→CAPTURED), cycle export JSON, off-screen rectangle drag, live telemetry panel — but there is only a design.md in add-ghost-calibration/. No spec.md, no tasks.md, no proposal.md exists under that change. Risk: the IDLE/RECORDING/REPOSITIONING/CAPTURED state transitions, SensorFrame/GhostFrame schemas, CalibrationExport format, and per-phase UI requirements have no normative specification. Any regression or port loses the expected contract.

title: E2E acceptance: /ghost rectangle matches main overlay movement
description:
After GhostMotionPipeline extraction, verify that both consumers produce identical visual behaviour for the same physical motion.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Open /ghost debug page and main camera view side by side (or switch between them)
2. Pan phone horizontally — rectangle and ghost image shift by the same magnitude in the same direction
3. Tilt phone vertically — same magnitude, same direction for both
4. Hold phone still — neither rectangle nor overlay drifts over 5 seconds
5. Motion gate threshold matches: small micro-movements suppress shift in both or neither

This issue is the only verifiable signal that the extraction actually unified behaviour rather than just restructuring code that continues to diverge at runtime.
close_reason: Manually verified: /ghost rectangle and main overlay produce identical shift magnitude and direction for yaw/pitch, no drift when stationary, motion gate suppression matches in both.

title: Add clampYawToViewport to GhostCalibrationPage
description: GhostCalibrationPage has no yaw clamping, causing unbounded yaw drift during long scans. GhostOverlayCanvas clamps via clampYawToViewport. Add same clamping to calibration page so both behave identically.

title: Fix scanAxis hard-coded to 'y' in GhostCalibrationPage
description: GhostCalibrationPage.onGyroReading hard-codes scanAxis to 'y' instead of calling getOrientation() like GhostOverlayCanvas does. This means horizontal scan axis is always gamma regardless of device orientation. Fix: replace literal 'y' with getOrientation()-based lookup matching canvas behavior.

title: Fix yaw accumulation during ghost-hidden blackout causing shift jumps
description:
During high-motion segments, the ghost is hidden repeatedly (7× in Photo 1→2, 5× in Photo 10→11) but yaw continues accumulating while the gate is closed. When the gate reopens the ghost jumps to the accumulated position (57px in Photo 10→11, yaw drifted 8.9°).

Fix: reset yawIntegral and pitchIntegral to 0 when the motion gate closes, consistent with the existing zeroVelocity() behavior for translation. This means the ghost always reappears at the current camera direction (0 shift) rather than jumping to accumulated drift.

Code location: ghostOverlayCanvas.ts:172 (gate-close handler in rafLoop). Change zeroVelocity(this.state) to also reset yawIntegral and pitchIntegral.

Acceptance: In Photo 1→2 and Photo 10→11 debug segments, ghost reappear shift jump is 0px (integral reset on hide).

title: Fix ghost position clamp causing yaw drift and jump on reappear
description:
The ghost overlay clamps its rendered X position to ±displayWidth/2 at the viewport edge. While clamped, yawIntegral in the state keeps accumulating, so when the camera pans back the ghost jumps to the over-accumulated position rather than sliding smoothly from the edge. Seen in Photo 2→3 (55px/78px jumps) and Photo 5→6 (clamped to -207px at shutter).

Fix: add clampYawToViewport(yawIntegral, hFovDeg) to ghostOverlay.ts that clamps the integral to [-tan(hFov/2), tan(hFov/2)] (display width cancels). Apply it in the RAF loop after rendering so the next gyro tick starts from the clamp boundary.

Code locations: ghostOverlay.ts — add clampYawToViewport() after computeShiftPx(). ghostOverlayCanvas.ts RAF loop — apply clamp after computing rotShiftPx.

Acceptance: debug replay ghost reappear after clamped-edge panning shows <5px jump.

title: Capture viewfinder UI: live preview + quality indicators + shutter
description: Why: this is the primary user-facing screen — users spend most of their time here taking shots. What: implement the capture screen with a full-screen video element showing the live camera feed; overlay quality warning badges (blur, tilt, exposure); steadiness indicator that goes green when the gate passes; ghost overlay canvas; shutter button that fires the capture flow and is disabled when not steady. Must work on Android Chrome in landscape.
notes: Post-tracer-bullet expansion ticket. Tracer-bullet slice mibilioteca-zvo now covers the first demoable one-capture UI happy path. Keep this issue focused on the broader production capture UX beyond the tracer bullet: live quality overlays, landscape polish, steady-state shutter ergonomics, and integration with ghost overlay / richer capture indicators.
close_reason: Steadiness gate (accel dep → feedAccel → shutter disabled + colored dot indicator), quality warning badges (blur/exposure via live frame polling), ghost overlay wiring (warningsEl preserved in viewfinder, setSnapshot on capture). 6 new tests. CSS for all new UI elements.

title: PWA app shell: manifest + install prompt + offline indicator
description: Why: the app must be installable as a PWA and must indicate offline status so users know uploads are queued. What: configure the PWA manifest (name, icons, display:standalone, start_url); implement the beforeinstallprompt handler for an in-app install button; add an offline/online indicator in the UI header. Confirm the app installs and loads offline after first visit.

title: Background Sync Service Worker (Workbox BackgroundSyncPlugin)
description: Why: uploads must continue when the user backgrounds the app or loses connectivity; Background Sync is the only reliable mechanism for this on Android Chrome. What: configure the Service Worker using vite-plugin-pwa and Workbox BackgroundSyncPlugin to queue POST /api/upload requests; set the Idempotency-Key: recordId header; mark records as uploading on dequeue. Update uploadState in IDB on SW success/failure message. Write a manual test checklist for background sync behavior.
notes:
Manual test checklist (required before closing — CI cannot exercise Background Sync):
1. Load app on Android Chrome over HTTPS
2. Take a photo while online — confirm status shows 'Saved ✓'
3. Go offline (airplane mode), take a photo — confirm 'Saved locally'
4. Restore network — confirm SW fires within ~30s and record appears uploaded (check DevTools > Application > Service Workers > Console for '[sw] upload' messages)
5. Force-kill browser tab mid-upload, reopen app — confirm stuck 'uploading' record is reset to 'failed' and retried on next sync
6. Verify Idempotency-Key header on duplicate sync attempts (check network tab — same recordId in header)

Background Sync API not available on Safari/iOS — those fall back to the online-event drain (mibilioteca-m7p)
close_reason: implemented: custom SW via injectManifest, drains IDB pending/failed on sync event, per-record error isolation, requestUploadSync wired after failed inline upload and on reconnect; 202 tests green; manual device test checklist added to issue notes

title: uploadState FSM + retry policy (5-attempt cap, terminal states)
description: Why: uploads can fail and must retry reliably without duplicating records or running forever. What: implement the upload FSM transitions: pending→uploading (picked up), uploading→uploaded (200), uploading→failed (retryable error: 429/5xx/network), failed→uploading (retry, max 5 total), failed→rejected (5th failure), uploading→rejected (terminal 4xx: 400/413/422). Write FSM as a pure transition function tested exhaustively against all response codes.

title: Shutter: capture → qualityChecks → CaptureRecord → IDB write
description: Why: this is the core capture operation that ties together camera, sensors, image processing, and storage into a single atomic user action. What: implement the shutter function — check steadiness gate; fire ImageCapture (or fallback); run quality checks on captured frame; build full CaptureRecord with all fields; write record JSON + image Blob + thumbnail Blob to IDB atomically; set uploadState='pending'. This is the most critical path in the app.
notes: Post-tracer-bullet expansion ticket. Tracer-bullet slices mibilioteca-lnf (minimal CaptureRecord factory), mibilioteca-xre (atomic capture persistence with cleanup), and mibilioteca-zvo (one-capture UI happy path) now cover the first end-to-end capture path. Keep this issue focused on the broader production capture pipeline beyond the tracer bullet: steadiness gate, full quality checks, richer sensor payloads, and complete shutter orchestration.

title: Session lifecycle: start/end + endedAt crash recovery
description: Why: a session must be opened before capture and cleanly closed after; but app crashes leave sessions without endedAt, which must be recoverable. What: implement startSession (writes CaptureSession to IDB with startedAt) and endSession (sets endedAt, triggers trace upload). On app start, detect sessions missing endedAt and infer it from max(capturedAt) across that session's records (crash recovery). Integration test the recovery path.

title: Unnamed quick-start scans get generated labels and preserved statuses
description:
## Why
Unnamed quick-start sessions must still be understandable and recoverable after the user returns home. This slice covers the homecoming lifecycle for unnamed sessions: the user should see a human-readable label instead of a UUID, and that same session should retain the correct **Pending**/**Exported** state when it reappears under **Previous scans**.

## End-to-end behavior
Unnamed scans display a generated timestamp label like **Scan May 21, 14:30** instead of a UUID in default UI. When the user returns home, that session appears under **Previous scans** with status **Pending** or **Exported** as appropriate.

## Scope
- Generated label rendering for unnamed scans in `src/scan/SessionsListView.ts`
- Shared formatter/helper for unnamed scan titles used by home, capture, and export-summary UI
- Previous-scan status rendering after backing out or after export
- Tests for generated labels and return-home status preservation

## Acceptance criteria
- Default home, capture, and export-summary UI hide UUIDs for unnamed scans and show generated **Scan …** labels instead
- Generated labels derive from `startedAt` and use a testable injected clock/formatter helper
- Returning home before export shows the session under **Previous scans** with status **Pending**
- Returning home after export shows the session under **Previous scans** with status **Exported**
- UUIDs remain available in details, debug views, and export metadata where already appropriate

## Traceability
- OpenSpec: `openspec/changes/add-quick-start-scan/specs/capture-start-ux/spec.md`
- Requirements: **Quick-start scan creation** / **Generated label for unnamed scans**; **Capture return preserves export status**
- Tasks: 2.7 plus the unnamed-label scenario under task group 2

## Delivery approach
Type: AFK

Apply TDD and Tidy First: add failing tests for label formatting and return-home statuses first, implement the smallest formatter/rendering changes, then tidy helper boundaries separately.

title: fix: tuning panel fully obscures ghost canvas with no way to observe ghost while adjusting
description: When the tuning panel is open on mobile (390x844 viewport), it covers the bottom half of the canvas. When any section is expanded (e.g. Orientation with 8 sliders), the panel takes the full visible screen and there is no way to see the ghost rectangle or observe the effect of parameter changes. Decision: implement option (c) — pin the canvas strip at the top of the screen and make the panel scroll below it. Options (a) transparent panel and (b) preview toggle are deferred. Measurement criterion: with panel open and Orientation section expanded, the ghost canvas must occupy >=100px of visible height at 390x844 viewport.
notes: File: src/ghost/TuningPanel.ts. OpenSpec: add-ghost-tuning-panel. Future options: (a) semi-transparent bottom-sheet, (b) 'preview' toggle that briefly hides panel — both deferred.

title: feat: show orientationSource field in telemetry panel for hybrid mode
description: GhostFrame already emits orientationSource ('gyro'|'absolute'|'hybrid'|'hybrid-fallback-gyro'|'hybrid-fallback-absolute') on every frame. This field is not displayed in the sensor telemetry panel on the ghost calibration page. In hybrid mode this makes the filter behavior completely opaque — users/developers cannot tell whether the gyro or absolute source is dominating on a given frame. Fix: add orientationSource to the telemetry readout, displayed after the Model line. Only show it when model is 'hybrid'.
notes: Files: src/ghost/GhostCalibrationPage.ts (telemetry display) and src/ghost/TuningPanel.ts (panel layout context). OpenSpec: add-ghost-tuning-panel. orientationSource is already emitted on every GhostFrame by the pipeline (see GhostFrame type). title: fix: tuning panel close button at bottom-left corner instead of inside panel
description: Playwright audit: the ✕ close button for the tuning panel is positioned at y=784 on an 844px tall screen (bottom-left corner, same position as the ⚙ gear button). This is non-standard — users expect a panel close affordance at the top of the panel. The bottom placement is also far from the panel content, breaking the spatial relationship. Fix: move the close button to the top-right corner inside the tuning panel header, alongside a panel title. Keep the gear button at the original bottom-left position for reopening.
notes: File: src/ghost/TuningPanel.ts. OpenSpec: add-ghost-tuning-panel. Acceptance: close button is inside the panel header at top-right; tapping it closes the panel.

title: fix: Still gain / Moving gain sliders visible in non-hybrid modes
description: Playwright evaluation confirmed that Still gain and Moving gain sliders (the complementary filter α knobs) are visible in the Orientation section even when the active model is 'gyro' or 'absolute'. These parameters only affect the hybrid complementary filter path and have no effect in other modes. Showing them in all modes confuses users about what is being tuned. Fix: conditionally render Still gain and Moving gain only when orientationModel === 'hybrid'.
notes: File: src/ghost/TuningPanel.ts. OpenSpec: add-ghost-tuning-panel. Conflict: mibilioteca-oste also touches the Orientation section; coordinate to avoid merge conflict. Screen readers cannot announce whether a section is open or closed. Fix: add aria-expanded='true/false' to each section toggle button, toggling on click. Also add a visible collapse/expand indicator (chevron icon) so the affordance is clear to sighted users too.
notes: File: src/ghost/TuningPanel.ts. OpenSpec: add-ghost-tuning-panel. Acceptance: each collapsible section has aria-expanded='true'/'false' matching visual state; chevron or +/- indicator is visible and updates on toggle.

title: fix: tuning panel sliders missing aria-label (all 19 range inputs)

Fix: add aria-label matching the visible text label (e.g. 'Gyro sensitivity', 'Still threshold') to each slider, or wrap each row in a fieldset/label structure.

title: Rename gate value 'dead-zone' to 'zupt' across codebase
description: The gate value 'dead-zone' describes the old binary suppression behavior. title: Replace AND dead-zone with L2 norm + ZUPT exponential decay
description: The current dead-zone uses AND logic (|ax|<0.05 AND |ay|<0.05), which lets ~40% of samples with a persistent ay bias of -0.039 escape because ay < -0.05. When they escape, velocity integrates fully causing upward drift in portrait. Replace with: (1) L2 norm threshold of 0.10 m/s² (~2σ above measured noise floor of 0.065 std) so ~95% of zero-motion samples are gated, and (2) exponential velocity decay (tau=200ms) instead of hard reset to zero, preventing discontinuities when noisy samples briefly escape the gate. This turns the open-loop accumulator into something with a corrective feedback path: stillness → velocity decays → position stops drifting.

title: Move dt computation before gate checks in feedGhostAccel

This is a prerequisite for adding ZUPT exponential decay (the decay factor is exp(-dt/tau)).

title: add-capture-metrics: implement estimateDisplacement and wire into shutter
description: Add `estimateDisplacement(samples: ImuSample[]): number` to `src/sensors/imuMath.ts` (created by mibilioteca-ybm with the `rotateVec` helper). Use trapezoidal integration with gravity subtraction via `grx/gry/grz` and quaternion rotation via `qx/qy/qz/qw`. Clamp result to 5 m maximum to guard against runaway values from tilt > 45°. Per-sample dt is capped at 50 ms to handle non-monotonic timestamps. Wire into `src/tracer/shutter.ts`: slice `imuTrace` between previous and current `capturedAtMonotonic` timestamps, call estimator, store in `qualityChecks.displacementMeters`. TDD: write failing tests (empty array → 0, single-element → 0, out-of-order timestamps → capped dt, stationary → near 0, constant accel → expected displacement, first capture → 0). Depends on the `rotateVec` helper (mibilioteca-ybm).

title: add-capture-metrics: create imuMath.ts with rotateVec helper
description: Create `src/sensors/imuMath.ts` and implement `rotateVec(v: Vec3, q: Quat): Vec3` as a pure helper for rotating a 3D vector by a quaternion. This function is needed by the displacement estimator. TDD: write failing unit tests (identity quaternion returns same vector; 90° yaw/pitch/roll rotations produce expected output), then implement. Place in `src/sensors/` to match the existing IMU module location pattern.

title: add-capture-metrics: improve exposure thresholds and propagate boolean flags
description: The exposure fraction thresholds are too loose for shelf-scanning conditions. Update `exposureFractions()` in `src/tracer/qualityChecks.ts`: raise overexposed clip to 240, underexposed floor to 15, add `meanLuma` accumulation, return `{ overexposed: boolean; underexposed: boolean; dark: boolean }` instead of raw fractions. Update `runQualityChecks()` to propagate `blurry`, `overexposed`, `underexposed`, `dark` boolean flags into the returned `QualityChecks` struct; wire through `src/tracer/shutter.ts`. TDD: write failing tests for each threshold (near-blown luma 241, crushed-shadow luma 14, dim-room mean < 50, normal range), then implement.

title: add-capture-metrics: fix laplacianVariance() GC allocation
description:
The current `laplacianVariance()` in `src/tracer/imageProcessing.ts` allocates a ~600 KB Float32Array `responses[]` on every call, causing 5–20 ms GC pauses on Android. Rewrite to accumulate `sum` and `sumSq` in-place without allocating the array. TDD: write test confirming the rewritten function produces identical results to the original, then implement the in-place accumulation.

Note: GC verification (Chrome DevTools Memory timeline on Android Chrome — 10 frames captured, confirm no GC events in the `laplacianVariance` span) is HITL. This step is required before shipping to users but is NOT required to close this ticket — the correctness test is the automated gate.

title: add-ghost-overlay: manual device acceptance test
description: Verify the ghost overlay behaves correctly end-to-end on a real Android device during a shelf scan. Acceptance criteria: (a) overlay invisible before first capture; (b) after first capture ghost appears at correct position; (c) 30° yaw rotation shifts overlay ~half-screen (~240 px at 65° hFOV on 480 px-wide view); (d) overlay hides during rapid repositioning; (e) no jitter when stationary. This is a manual-only test — no automated test possible.
close_reason: Manually verified on device: overlay invisible before capture, appears at correct position after capture, tracks rotation correctly, hides during rapid repositioning, no jitter when stationary.

title: add-capture-metrics: add boolean quality fields and rename stepCountSincePrev
description: Type foundation work required before any metrics can be implemented. (a) Add `blurry: boolean`, `overexposed: boolean`, `underexposed: boolean`, `dark: boolean` to `qualityChecks` in `CaptureRecord` and `CaptureRecordInput` in `src/tracer/capture.ts`. (b) Audit `src/tracer/shutter.ts` and `src/tracer/qualityChecks.ts` for any assignment to `stepCountSincePrev` to confirm it has never been populated with meaningful data. (c) Rename `stepCountSincePrev` → `displacementMeters` in both types and update all callsites. This is a refactoring task — update types and callsites, ensure tests still pass.

title: add-ghost-overlay: guard setSnapshot() against null grabFrame() result
description:
grabFrame() is asynchronous and may return null if the track is ended or the canvas context is lost (e.g. user navigates away mid-capture). In `CaptureView.takePhoto()` (`src/tracer/CaptureView.ts`), guard the `ghostOverlay.setSnapshot()` call — skip the call and retain the previous ghost content when grabFrame returns null; do not reset the yaw accumulator. TDD: write failing tests for both null-grabFrame cases, then add the guard:
1. WHEN grabFrame returns null after at least one prior capture THEN previous snapshot is retained
2. WHEN grabFrame returns null on the first capture THEN ghost canvas remains hidden

title: add-ghost-overlay: implement all-axis motion gating in rafLoop
description: The ghost overlay must hide during rapid camera motion to avoid blur-on-blur confusion. Extend `GhostOverlayState` to track latest angular velocity magnitude across all axes (gx, gy, gz); extend `feedGhostGyro()` to accept all three axes. In `GhostOverlayCanvas.rafLoop()`, hide the canvas when stored |ω| > 0.5 rad/s on any axis; restore when ≤ 0.5 and at least one snapshot has been drawn. TDD order: failing tests → implementation. Files: `src/sensors/ghostOverlay.ts`, `src/sensors/ghostOverlayCanvas.ts`.

title: add-ghost-overlay: clamp shift to ±videoWidth/2 in computeShiftPx()
description: The ghost overlay spec requires shift to be clamped to ±videoWidth/2 to prevent the overlay from panning off screen. Extend `computeShiftPx()` in `src/sensors/ghostOverlay.ts` to apply the clamp after computing the pixel shift. TDD: write failing tests first (large yaw → clamped to ±videoWidth/2; small yaw → unclamped), then implement the clamp in the function.

title: Research: IMU-derived shelf displacement between ZUPT anchors
description: ZUPT anchoring is already designed (each CaptureRecord has zupt:true). We need to research how to integrate accelerometer readings between stationary moments to estimate linear displacement (meters along shelf). Covers sensor fusion options (Kalman/complementary filter), dead reckoning accuracy on phone-grade sensors, and practical accuracy validation approach.

title: Research: image quality scoring for captured frames
description: We need an algorithm to score blur, sharpness, and exposure for frames captured via getUserMedia+canvas. This research should identify the best algorithm for real-time quality feedback on a 320×240 downscaled grabFrame(), define thresholds for 'too blurry to use', and assess JS/WASM feasibility for in-browser computation.

description: Why: without persist(), Chrome may LRU-evict IDB blobs before upload completes, causing silent data loss. What: call navigator.storage.persist() at session start; show a persistent warning banner if denied; check navigator.storage.estimate() and warn if < 500 MB available; pause capture and show a blocking warning if quota is exhausted mid-session.
close_reason: Added storage persistence request, quota warnings, and exhausted-quota capture block

title: IMU trace upload (POST /api/upload/trace)
description: Why: the backend requires the full IMU trace Blob after each session ends for spatial alignment. What: implement trace upload — read trace Blob from IDB by sessionId; POST to /api/upload/trace as application/octet-stream with X-Session-Id, X-Scan-Id, X-Sample-Rate-Hz, X-Fields headers. Handle 400/413/500. Trigger after endSession.

title: online-event drain fallback loop
description: Why: Background Sync is Chromium-only; iOS and some edge cases need a fallback that drains the pending upload queue when the device comes online. What: implement an online event listener that queries records by uploadState='pending', uploads them sequentially using POST /api/upload with Idempotency-Key, and updates uploadState through the FSM. Must coexist safely with the SW background sync (no double-upload: check uploadState before each request).
close_reason: Implemented online-event upload drain fallback with shared queue drain, persisted upload claiming to avoid SW/fallback double-upload, and tests.

title: motionWindow extraction from active IMU trace
description: Why: CaptureRecord.motionWindow needs a 7-field excerpt of the continuous trace centered on the shot timestamp for per-record quality use without loading the full Blob. What: implement extractMotionWindow(trace: Float32Array, shotMonotonicMs: number, windowMs: 200): motionWindow samples array. Pure function, unit tested with a synthetic trace.
notes: Function signature: extractMotionWindow(trace: Float32Array, shotMs: number, windowMs = 200): Float32Array. Test cases must cover at minimum: (1) shot mid-trace — window is symmetric; (2) shot at trace start — window is right-padded or truncated; (3) shot at trace end — window is left-padded or truncated. windowMs=200 is a default, not a fixed constant.

title: Clock sync: initial + mid-session re-sync (GET /api/scan/:id/time)
description: Why: clockOffsetMs can drift over a long session; re-syncing keeps cross-device event ordering accurate. What: implement a re-sync call to GET /api/scan/:id/time that fires every 30 min or when Date.now() - performance.now() diverges from the initial baseline by > 500 ms. Update clockOffsetMs in IDB and session state on re-sync. Done: Vitest fake-timer test asserts re-sync triggers at 30min interval and on 500ms drift.
close_reason: Implemented GET /api/scan/:id/time clock re-sync with 30-minute scheduling, 500ms drift checks, IDB session update, in-memory onUpdate callback, and tests.

title: shortCode generator + clockOffsetMs pure functions + tests
description: Why: shortCode generation and clock offset math are small pure functions used in scan creation and session join respectively; they need tests before being wired into the API layer. What: implement shortCode() that generates '4 letters + dash + 3 alphanumeric (no I/O/0/1)'; implement clockOffsetMs(serverTimeMs) = Date.now() - serverTimeMs. Unit test both, including disambiguation of excluded chars.

title: Quality checks runner (exposure, tilt, blur thresholds + warnings)
description: Why: the UI must show real-time warnings when a shot is about to be taken with poor quality; the runner computes all checks from a captured frame and current sensor state. What: implement runQualityChecks(imageData, sensorState) that returns a QualityChecks object with all fields. Apply spec thresholds: laplacianVariance < 80 blurry, overexposedFraction > 0.05, underexposedFraction > 0.05, tiltDegrees > 15. Unit test each threshold boundary.
close_reason: Implemented runQualityChecks + qualityWarnings with THRESHOLDS. 16 tests covering all boundaries. Ro5u pass — fixed else-if defensive issue and added positive laplacian test.

title: laplacianVariance + makeThumbnail pure functions + tests
description: Why: blur detection and thumbnail generation are reusable pure functions that the shutter pipeline calls on every shot; they must be correct and fast. What: implement laplacianVariance(imageData: ImageData): number using a 3x3 Laplacian kernel on the luma channel; implement makeThumbnail(blob: Blob, maxEdgePx: 640): Promise<Blob> using canvas drawImage + toBlob('image/jpeg', 0.85). Both are pure and independently unit-tested. No browser test required — use OffscreenCanvas or a test stub.
close_reason: laplacianVariance (3x3 Laplacian kernel on luma) and makeThumbnail (injectable canvas deps) implemented with 9 unit tests

title: Steadiness gate (ZUPT: low-variance accelerometer check)
description: Why: every CaptureRecord carries zupt:true, which means the shutter must be blocked unless the device is stationary. What: implement a steadiness gate that computes rolling variance of the linear accelerometer over a 200ms window; blocks the shutter button when variance exceeds a threshold; sets steadyAtCapture:true in qualityChecks when the shot fires. Write a pure feedAccel function tested with synthetic stable and shaky inputs.

title: IMU trace recorder (Float32Array, 14 fields, 50-60 Hz)
description: Why: the backend needs a continuous 14-field IMU stream per session for spatial alignment; this must record at sensor rate without blocking the UI thread. What: implement a trace recorder that subscribes to all six sensors, appends samples to a growing Float32Array buffer (fields: t,ax,ay,az,gx,gy,gz,qx,qy,qz,qw,grx,gry,grz), and on session end serializes to a Blob and writes to the traces IDB store. Track pauseGaps when the page is hidden. Pure feedSample function that appends one 14-float row; integration test covers round-trip to IDB.

title: Generic Sensor permission flow + feature detection
description: Why: sensors require a user gesture and may not be available on all devices; the app must detect what is available and request permissions before starting capture. What: implement a sensor probe that checks window for Accelerometer, Gyroscope, AbsoluteOrientationSensor, GravitySensor; calls requestPermission() on iOS; and returns a capability map used to decide which fields of CaptureRecord.motion and CaptureRecord.orientation to populate. Degrade gracefully when sensors are unavailable.
close_reason: probeSensors + detectSensorDeps in src/sensors/probe.ts; 8 tests covering Generic Sensor API, iOS permission gate, and graceful degradation

title: IDB CRUD: traces, previewFrames, and previewBlobs stores
description: Why: the IMU trace Blob and optional preview frames need their own store accessors, separate from the main capture record flow. What: typed IDB access functions for traces (get, put by sessionId), previewFrames (get, put), and previewBlobs (get, put). Write integration tests confirming the blobRef identity contract (trace blobRef === sessionId, previewFrame blobRef === frameId).
close_reason: getTrace/putTrace, getPreviewFrame/putPreviewFrame, getPreviewBlob/putPreviewBlob added with 6 integration tests

title: ImageCapture + canvas snapshot degradation ladder
description: Why: ImageCapture.takePhoto() often returns video-resolution on Android Chrome — the client must fall back gracefully without breaking the capture flow. What: implement the degradation ladder: try ImageCapture.takePhoto(); if it returns a Blob smaller than the expected resolution, fall back to canvas.toBlob() from the live video frame. Record sourceApi ('ImageCapture' | 'CanvasSnapshot') in CaptureRecord.image. Test with a mock that simulates low-res takePhoto response.

title: Add ILogger interface to debug/logger
description: debug/logger is a concrete singleton imported by 14+ modules, making it impossible to inject test doubles. Add an ILogger interface that the concrete DebugLogger implements — this is the minimum needed for testability without a wide DI refactor. Full injection across all 14 callers is out of scope; the interface alone unblocks test isolation in new code and extracted classes.

title: Fix translation axis mapping in landscape orientation
description: In landscape mode, the accelerometer X axis becomes screen-vertical and Y axis becomes screen-horizontal, but feedGhostAccel always maps ax→dx_m (lateral) and ay→dy_m (vertical). This produces wrong translation shift direction in landscape — lateral pans accumulate in dy_m instead of dx_m. The gyro path already handles this via scanAxis, but the translation path has no equivalent rotation. Fix: detect landscape orientation in onMotionReading() (same screen.orientation.type check as onGyroReading) and swap/negate ax/ay in AccelSample before feeding. Sign convention for landscape-primary vs landscape-secondary differs, so needs device testing to verify.

title: Upload reliability: production-grade Background Sync + queueing strategy
description:
## Why this issue exists
The tracer bullet implemented a direct stub upload attempt and a basic online-event drain fallback (mibilioteca-m7p) and Background Sync SW (mibilioteca-z6p). These cover the happy path and basic offline recovery. Production reliability — retry storms, quota limits, conflict resolution for multi-device uploads, and full Background Sync lifecycle testing — was deferred.

## What needs to be done
Audit the current upload queue and Background Sync implementation against production failure scenarios:
- Retry storm prevention (exponential back-off with jitter)
- Upload quota / storage pressure handling
- Conflict resolution when the same capture is uploaded from multiple paths (SW + fallback)
- Full Background Sync lifecycle on Android Chrome (registration, firing, success/failure callbacks)
- Verify claiming logic prevents double-upload under race conditions

## Ref
openspec/changes/add-tracer-bullet/design.md — Non-Goals: 'Upload queueing beyond a direct stub upload attempt'; 'Background Sync reliability work'

title: Collaboration: multi-user scan join flow
description:
## Why this issue exists
The tracer bullet proved the single-device happy path (one device, one scan, one capture). Multi-user collaboration — where a second device joins an existing scan via an invite code or link — was explicitly deferred as a non-goal.

## What needs to be done
Design and implement the multi-device join flow: scan owner shares a join code or link; joining device receives the Scan ID and authenticates; both devices write captures to the same scan in IndexedDB / on the server; UI reflects multi-participant state.

## Out of scope
- Backend pairing/invite infrastructure (depends on real backend ticket)
- Real-time sync (may be a separate concern)

## Ref
openspec/changes/add-tracer-bullet/design.md — Non-Goals: 'Multi-user join flows'

title: iOS InputFileCapture fallback

title: Real-time multi-user collaboration: live shared capture sessions
description: Allow multiple participants to capture the same shelf simultaneously with a shared session view. Requires server clock anchoring, account/auth system, live state sync, and the backend scan/join API endpoints. This is explicitly deferred post-MVP — the bundle-first approach validates capture quality before this complexity is warranted.

title: Automatic backup: auto-upload bundles or records when connectivity available
description: Post-MVP, give users the option to automatically back up captured data when the device is online, rather than requiring manual export and transfer. Options include: auto-bundle upload to Drive/similar, or background per-record upload via the backend API. Must integrate with export state tracking and not delete source IndexedDB artifacts until backup is confirmed.

title: Multi-device merge: combine captures from multiple devices into one scan
description: When multiple phones capture the same shelf in parallel, their records need to be merged into a single ordered scan. MVP treats each bundle/session as locally ordered by capturedAtMonotonic. Post-MVP, this requires either fiducial/tie shots for spatial anchoring or backend-assisted merge using server clock offsets and spatial overlap detection.

title: Backend ingest: per-record upload after MVP bundle validation
description: Once bundle artifacts have been validated against downstream processing needs, implement per-record upload to the backend API. The capture client should unpack bundle records and upload them individually via POST /api/upload (with Idempotency-Key for safe retry). Activate BackgroundSyncPlugin and online-event drain for resilient delivery under field connectivity conditions. This work must not begin until at least one bundle has been validated manually end-to-end.
